about.heading: About
about.paragraph1: I'm a frontend developer with 4 years at Infosys, mostly on enterprise banking portals for UAE and KSA clients. Most of my work sits at the intersection of three constraints that don't show up in tutorials: strict role-based access control, data that has to stay correct under real-time updates, and performance budgets for users on inconsistent mobile connections.
about.paragraph2: I've spent the last two years moving from building components to owning a full frontend module — from architecture decisions down to the caching strategy that keeps it fast.
about.paragraph3: Based in India. Open to full-time roles in UAE, KSA, and India.

jobpilot.title: JobPilot — AI resume analysis & optimization platform
jobpilot.problem: A full-stack platform that evaluates a resume against a specific job description and generates a structured ATS-style analysis: missing keywords, strengths, weaknesses, and concrete recommendations — built and shipped end to end, not a prototype.

decisions.title: Structured output validation with Zod before anything reaches the UI
decisions.desc: LLM output is parsed against a strict schema before rendering, so a malformed or incomplete AI response never breaks the analysis screen — the UI only ever sees data it can trust.

decisions.title: Streamed AI responses via the Vercel AI SDK
decisions.desc: Resume analysis takes a few seconds end to end, so results stream in as they're generated instead of the user staring at a blank spinner.

decisions.title: Secure auth with persistent analysis history
decisions.desc: Built on NextAuth/Better Auth so users can log in and come back to past resume analyses instead of losing results after a single session.

decisions.title: MySQL and Prisma for the data layer
decisions.desc: Resumes, job descriptions, and generated analyses are all persisted relationally, which made building the history feature straightforward rather than bolted on.

jobpilot.whatNextBody: Add caching for repeat resume/job-description pairs so re-running an analysis doesn't hit the LLM API again for the same input.

pulseboard.title: PulseBoard — role-based frontend architecture
pulseboard.problem: A personal project built to explore a pattern I use at work but can't show publicly: a dashboard where different roles see different data and actions, real-time KPIs stay correct, and table and chart views hold up under large paginated datasets — without the codebase turning into scattered permission checks as features get added.

decisions.title: RBAC at three levels — route, component, and action
decisions.desc: Permissions are checked at the point of use instead of a single top-level route guard, which prevents a hidden button from staying reachable via a stale cached page.

decisions.title: Server state separated from UI state, via React Query
decisions.desc: KPI and user data is cached and revalidated independently from UI-only state like open modals and filters, avoiding the classic conflict of using one store for both.

decisions.title: Schema-driven validation with Zod
decisions.desc: Form validation lives in one schema the UI can share, so refactoring a form doesn't silently break validation elsewhere.

decisions.title: Paginated tables and charts
decisions.desc: Designed to handle large datasets without loading everything client-side, keeping interaction smooth as data volume grows.

pulseboard.whatNextBody: Add optimistic updates for the KPI actions instead of waiting on a full refetch — right now a slow connection makes the dashboard feel less responsive than it should.
